sentences.text: This matter is taken up through a hybrid arrangement.

2. The petitioner, who is in custody in connection with Malkangiri P.S. Case No. 136 of 2024,
corresponding to G.R. Case No. 171 of 2024, pending before the learned S.D.J.M., Malkangiri, and registered for the alleged commission of offences under Section 420,408, 409,467,468,471,506, and 120-B of IPC, has filed this petition seeking release on bail.
3. The brief fact of the case is that the informant was working as the operation head in Axis bank at Malkangiri.

Opposite ... on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51258576/
1 involved in fraudulent disbursement of gold loan in the name of different borrowers.
They received less quantity of gold from the borrowers but showed huge quantity in gold deposit receipt.
They also provided inflated gold valuation certificate to facilitate gold loan thereby causing loss of amount Rs.83,80,000/- to the bank.
4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that the Petitioner has already spent 9 months in the custody.
Hence, he submits that the Petitioner may be enlarged on bail.
5. Learned counsel for the State vehemently opposes the bail prayer of the Petitioner.

6. Without delving into the intricacies of the case or the merits of the allegations, and in light of the facts and circumstances at hand, this Court is of the view that the Petitioner should be granted bail by the learned court in seisin over the matter, subject to stringent terms and conditions.

The conditions are as follows:-
i. The petitioner shall deposit his passport, if any, before the local Police Station; ii.
The petitioner shall appear before the local Police Station on every Monday in between 10 A.M. to 1.00 P.M. iii.

The petitioner shall not indulge himself in any criminal offence while on bail;
iii. The petitioner shall not tamper with the evidence or intimidate the prosecution witnesses in any manner; and iv.

The petitioner shall plant 100 saplings of local varieties, such as mango, neem,
tamarind, etc., around his village on government land, community land, or private land in the possession of the petitioner or her family members.

In the event that suitable land is unavailable,
the Revenue Authority shall assist in identifying land for the plantation.

Violation of any of the above conditions shall lead to the cancellation of the bail.
7.
The I.I.C. of the concerned police station, in coordination with the local Forest Officer, shall monitor whether the petitioner has planted the saplings as required.

8. It is further directed that the petitioner shall file an affidavit before the local police station,
confirming that the saplings have been planted and that the petitioner will maintain them for a period of two years.
9. The District Nursery/District Forest Officer (D.F.O.) shall extend assistance to the petitioner by supplying the necessary saplings.
10. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
